brief: PNC reports September 2026 final demand PPI rose 1.3% month over month and 6.3% year over year. Goods PPI jumped 2.6%, the largest monthly increase since the data series began in November 2009, reversing a moderation trend that had averaged -0.3% per month since May. Energy PPI drove much of the move, up 10.8% for the month (topping March's 10.5% gain, which followed the U.S.-Iran military conflict) and up 35.6% year over year (topping May's 32.3% year-ago high). PNC ties the September CPI's gasoline bounce (+9.1% m/m) to the energy PPI spike and argues the energy acceleration will feed through to goods production costs, dampening any return to cooler goods inflation. Core PPI, excluding food and energy, also accelerated to 0.7% from 0.2% in August, which PNC says shows broader inflation pressure independent of the energy bounce. PNC concludes the report supports additional Fed tightening and projects two more 25 basis point Fed Funds hikes through early 2027, while noting higher prices could also slow consumer demand growth and ease some of the inflationary pressure the Fed is addressing.
